svg.title: / and then * typed at the start of row 4 of countdown.c at 06.03: the rows scanned again, one after another, until a row ends the way it did before
svg.text: hl of each row as the scan leaves it; the screen is drawn once, after the key

g.title: Before: rows 1 and 2 end inside the comment that row 1 opens; row 3 closes it, and every row after that ends outside one.
/ typed at the start of row 4: the row is scanned again. "/#" opens nothing, and the row ends outside a comment, as before: nothing below it is touched.
* typed: row 4 is scanned again. Now "/*" opens a comment that does not close on this row: it ends inside one, where it ended outside before. So the row below starts differently: it is next.
Row 5, empty, starts inside the comment and has nothing to close it: it ends inside, and it did not before. On to row 6.
Row 6 is all comment now: every character cyan, and it ends inside. Changed: on to row 7.
Row 7: the string and the number are part of the comment too. Changed: on to row 8.
Row 8 the same. On to row 9.
Row 9: the // after the tab is inside the comment, so it is part of it; it opens nothing. Ends inside: on to row 10.
Row 10: "/*" inside a comment opens nothing, and "*/" closes it. The row ends outside a comment, as it did before: the scan stops here.
The frame is drawn: rows 4 to 10 in the comment's colour. Rows 11 and 12 were not scanned again, and keep their colours: nothing above them ends differently.
